name: create_incident
title: Create incident
description: Creates a new incident in the incident management system and notifies the on-call engineer of the affected service. Use this tool when a production alert has fired or a customer reports an outage. The incident is created in the 'triggered' state and can later be acknowledged or resolved with the other tools of this server. Required fields are the title, the severity and the affected service. Optionally provide a longer description, labels, a list of responders to add immediately, and a link to the monitoring dashboard that triggered the alert. The tool returns the incident id, a public URL and the escalation policy that was applied. It does not close or modify existing incidents, and it refuses to create a duplicate when an open incident with the same title and service already exists. Rate limit: at most 30 incidents per minute per API key. If the incident management system is in maintenance mode the tool fails with a retryable error and the caller should wait at least 60 seconds before trying again. The tool never pages more than 10 responders in one call; use the escalation tools for larger groups. All timestamps are interpreted as UTC unless an explicit offset is given, and free-text fields are stored as Markdown and rendered on the incident page. Attachments are not supported; link to external evidence instead.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of what is broken, for example 'Checkout API returns 502'.

severity.description: Impact level. sev1 means full outage or data loss, sev4 means cosmetic issue.

service_id.description: Identifier of the affected service in the service catalog.

description.description: Longer free-text description with symptoms, first occurrence and what was already tried.

responders.description: User ids or schedule ids to page immediately, in addition to the default escalation policy.

dashboard_url.description: Link to the dashboard or alert that triggered the incident.

notify_stakeholders.description: When true, also posts a status update to the stakeholder channel.

assignee_team.description: Team that should own the incident. Defaults to the owner of the affected service.

runbook_url.description: Link to the runbook that applies to this kind of incident.

customer_impact.description: Estimated customer impact, used for prioritisation and status page text.

affected_regions.description: Regions where the problem is observed.

started_at.description: When the problem started, if known. Defaults to the time of the call.

external_ticket_id.description: Id of a related ticket in the issue tracker, linked from the incident.

url.description: Public URL of the incident page.

escalation_policy.description: Name of the escalation policy that was applied.

paged.description: Ids of the users that were paged.

status_page_url.description: URL of the status page entry, present only when notify_stakeholders was true.
